PRODUCT MENTAL MODELPAGE 03 / 30

What Skyvern solves

Skyvern automates real browser work by combining language-model reasoning with browser-control tools instead of relying only on fixed selectors.

The core problem

Traditional automation scripts often target a website through hard-coded CSS selectors or XPath expressions. A redesign, renamed button, or changed page structure can break the script.

Skyvern accepts a goal in natural language, observes the page, chooses actions, executes them in a real browser, and checks whether the goal has been reached.

SCRIPT-FIRST

Selector automation

  • Developer identifies exact selectors.
  • Script follows predefined paths.
  • Layout changes can invalidate locators.
  • Each website may need custom logic.
SKYVERN APPROACH

Goal-driven automation

  • User describes the intended outcome.
  • Agent observes interactive elements and page context.
  • LLM selects an action from available tools.
  • Browser state is re-read to confirm progress.

What this enables

Form fillingData extractionLogin + 2FAFile downloadingMulti-page navigationReusable workflowsAPI / spreadsheet handoffs
Do not overclaim the AI
Skyvern reduces dependence on brittle selectors; it does not make every site identical or guarantee success on every page. Websites can still block automation, load unpredictably, require human approval, or expose ambiguous controls. The code includes budgets, recovery paths, and terminal statuses for that reason.

SYSTEM OVERVIEWPAGE 05 / 30

Platform architecture: how components connect

Skyvern is a layered application. The agent is only one layer; it depends on API, browser, LLM, database, artifact, credential, and integration services.

Conceptual architecture synthesized from the repository’s application container, FastAPI app, services, engines, browser manager and storage classes.

Execution plane

Request handling, workflow preparation, run dispatch, block execution, browser acquisition, AI reasoning, action calls and goal checks.

Platform plane

Organizations, auth, database, run history, credentials, schedules, storage, logs, telemetry, integrations and webhooks.

Why separation matters
The browser does not own the workflow definition, and the LLM does not directly own the browser. The workflow/agent layer coordinates them; browser actions pass through browser abstractions; platform services persist and govern the run.

END-TO-END FLOWPAGE 06 / 30

Full request lifecycle: from goal to run result

The important sequence is: accept → validate → prepare → dispatch → execute → persist → report.

01 · Entry

A user submits a task or agent run through the UI, Python/TypeScript SDK, REST API, or an MCP-facing tool.

02 · Authentication and validation

FastAPI route dependencies identify the organization, check auth, parse Pydantic request models, and validate parameters and run options.

03 · Prepare the run

workflow_service.prepare_workflow resolves the workflow version, checks inputs, and creates/persists a workflow-run record.

04 · Dispatch

The executor/worker claims work. Run context is populated with organization, workflow, parameters, browser/session, and budgets.

05 · Execute

ForgeAgent dispatches blocks/tasks. Browser-based blocks obtain a browser; selected engine runs the step or Task V3 tool loop.

06 · Persist evidence

Block outputs, step/action information, status, screenshots, recordings, downloads and artifacts are saved.

07 · Finalize and notify

Run status becomes terminal, outputs are made available, and configured webhook delivery can notify the caller.

Run lifecycle statuses
The source defines created, queued, running, paused, completed, failed, terminated, timed_out, and canceled. Paused is meaningful when a human-interaction block waits for a person.

CORE AGENT WORKFLOWPAGE 07 / 30

The browser-agent loop: observe, reason, act, verify

The core cycle repeats until a goal is reached or the run stops for a defined reason.

Observe

Capture page state: visible controls, labels, values, options, frames and, when enabled, screenshot evidence.

Reason

Give the model the user goal, current observations, prior messages and allowed tools. Ask it to choose the next action.

Act

Dispatch a browser operation such as click, type, select, hover, scroll, upload or navigate.

Verify

Re-observe the page and judge whether the intended state change or final goal is supported by evidence.

The repository documentation describes the standard agent pass as a screenshot/page read, model decision, Playwright execution, and goal check. Task V3 uses a more specific persistent tool-call loop described on pages 9–11.

LEGACY / CONCEPTUAL ARCHITECTUREPAGE 08 / 30

Skyvern 2.0: Planner, Task, and Validator

The README’s 2.0 diagram is a useful explanation of the agent swarm idea: break a large goal into steps, execute each step, and validate the outcome.

PLANNER

Break the goal down

Converts a user request into an ordered set of subtasks. It receives feedback when a validation step finds that the overall goal is not complete.

TASK

Do one step

Perceives the current website, identifies elements, asks the model which action is appropriate, and executes the chosen action through the browser automation layer.

VALIDATOR

Check the result

Judges whether the requested goal or subgoal is satisfied. A negative result becomes feedback for another planning/execution pass.

Interpretation warning
This image and the README describe Skyvern 2.0’s architecture. The same exact three boxes should not be treated as the call graph for every engine in this repository. Task V3, for example, uses a persistent LLM conversation with in-process browser tools.

Why the design was useful

It separates three reasoning responsibilities: what should happen next, how to interact with this page, and whether the result is good enough. That separation helps explain complex browser tasks to learners even when the implementation evolves.

CURRENT SOURCE PATHPAGE 09 / 30

Task V3: the native persistent tool-loop

Task V3 runs an entire supported task through one persistent model conversation that perceives and acts using raw browser tools.

What the source explicitly says

  • engine.py assembles prompts, tools, and the tool-loop call.
  • The caller supplies a PageProvider and a concrete LLMCaller.
  • The page is resolved fresh on each tool call, rather than binding the loop to one stale page.
  • Browser tools are in-process raw-DOM/selector operations. The code explains why it avoids a separate-process MCP transport here.
  • The caller maps the returned LoopOutcome to task status and output.

Dispatch rule

Inside ForgeAgent.execute_step, the V3 path requires the selected engine to be skyvern-3.0, the task block to support V3 (or a bare task), and the DISABLE_TASK_V3 switch not to disable it. Unsupported block types or a disabled flag fall back to the step engine.

Mental model
Think of Task V3 as one model dialogue that calls browser tools, rather than a chain where every browser step starts a brand-new LLM “act” request. The persistent conversation retains the task context between tool calls.

RAW DOM + IN-PROCESS BROWSER TOOLSPAGE 10 / 30

Task V3 tools: how the model touches a page

The model cannot inspect the page unless it calls a tool. It receives a compact observation and then targets elements with references.

observe()

Returns visible interactive elements with a reference, label, type, current value and (for selects) options.

action(ref=N)

Use the exact reference from the latest observation to click, type, hover, select, scroll, press keys, or upload.

tool result

Reports success, failure, returned data, and relevant browser evidence to the same model conversation.

Why reference IDs?

A ref such as ref=12 is an address for an element from a particular page snapshot. It is safer than guessing a CSS selector from a label. If the element disappears or becomes ambiguous, the tool can refuse rather than silently click a different element. Re-observe after the page changes.

PageProvider matters

A click can open a popup or a new tab. Resolving the working page on every tool call lets the next action follow the browser’s current working page instead of continuing against a stale tab.

Batching is important
The Task V3 system prompt instructs the model to observe a page once, then batch independent field fills and selections into one turn before triggering a page reload. This can reduce tool calls and latency on long forms.

Vision is conditional: screenshots are sent only when the selected model supports vision and the run’s screenshot policy enables them. The tool-loop also works from compact DOM observations.

DO NOT TRUST A CLAIM ALONEPAGE 11 / 30

Finish, verification, and failure handling

Task V3’s finish tool is surrounded by bounded verification and stop gates to reduce false success and premature failure.

Model calls finish(completed)Is the page stable? Is the completion evidence grounded? Is a submission still pending? Has a required file landed?
Completion gatesMay defer and ask the model to re-observe; may block completion if a required condition is not satisfied.
Final outcomeCaller maps the final LoopOutcome to task status, reason, and extracted output.

Key protections visible in source

  • Page settling: a completed claim can be deferred until page fingerprints match across samples.
  • Failure evidence: after recent submit/captcha activity, a failed verdict may be held for another observation.
  • Submission watch: a still-pending submit control can prevent immediate completion.
  • Completion gate: customer/workflow criteria can veto completion if there is budget to continue.
  • Runaway limits: turn, tool-call, token, action-step, and wall-clock limits bound the loop.
80default max turns
300default max tool calls
1,800 sdefault wall-clock guard
1.5Mdefault token backstop
Terminal meanings
completed = goal accepted; failed = execution could not finish; terminated = agent/workflow concludes the goal cannot or should not continue; timed_out = time limit; canceled = user/system cancellation. These are not interchangeable.

ENGINE ROUTINGPAGE 12 / 30

Engines: which reasoning path is selected?

The codebase supports multiple engine IDs. The engine is selected per run or per browser block, subject to block support and configuration.

Engine valueWhat the repo labels itNotes
skyvern-1.0Skyvern 1.0Legacy step-engine path.
skyvern-2.0Skyvern 2.0Legacy; existing blocks can remain on it.
skyvern-3.0Skyvern 3.0Recommended in current Studio docs; supports native Task V3 for eligible tasks.
openai-cuaOpenAI CUAComputer-use agent route.
anthropic-cuaAnthropic CUAComputer-use agent route.
ui-tarsUI-TARSSeparate computer-use engine path.

What happens when V3 is not available?

In ForgeAgent.execute_step, Skyvern checks engine value, block eligibility, and the disable switch. A supported V3 task runs once through _execute_task_v3; unsupported blocks or disabled V3 continue via the step engine. This compatibility path is important when debugging mixed workflows.

Default values are context-dependent
The schema’s RunEngine enum and request defaults, Studio’s Cloud default for newly created agents, and a block’s saved engine selection are separate concerns. Check the actual run/block config instead of assuming one default applies everywhere.

THE EXECUTION ENVIRONMENTPAGE 13 / 30

Browser runtime: Playwright, Chromium, CDP

Skyvern controls a real browser through browser-manager abstractions. The browser is a resource with a lifecycle, not a static web page object.

chromium-headful

Visible browser window. In Docker it can be drawn on a virtual display.

chromium-headless

No visible window. Some websites may behave differently or block headless browsers.

cdp-connect

Connect to an existing Chrome using the Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint, or launch an installed Chrome configuration.

Key browser modules

  • RealBrowserManager — acquires and manages browser state for a run/session.
  • browser_factory.py — browser launch/connect plumbing, headers, downloads, profile/session behavior.
  • browser_state.py — tracks browser context, page, navigation and state.
  • skycdp/ — CDP transport/facade interfaces for browser/page operations.
  • playwright_input.py — browser input integration around Playwright.

Sessions vs profiles

A browser session is a live browser with tabs, cookies and current state. A browser profile is saved reusable browser state (cookies/storage) that can seed later runs. A session is temporary; a profile is intended to be reused.

Why this matters
A task may need to preserve a login across blocks or runs. Session/profile selection, browser leases and page reacquisition determine whether the automation resumes in the expected browser context.

SCRAPING + DOM INSPECTIONPAGE 14 / 30

Webeye perception layer: turning pages into evidence

The webeye package captures and transforms browser state into information an agent can reason over.

Browser pageLive DOM, frames, viewport, network and page URL
ScraperReads DOM and interactive controls, discovers child frames and builds structured element trees
NormalizationTrims attributes, builds stable element identities, redacts values where required
Agent observationCompact elements / DOM text and optional screenshot sent to the model

Important files

webeye/scraper/scraper.pyScrape page and frames; build an interactable element tree; trim output.
webeye/dom_inspection.pyDOM inspection helpers.
webeye/utils/dom.pyDOM utility functions.
webeye/utils/page.pyPage/frame helpers and privacy masking helpers.
forge/taskv3/turn_dom.pyTask V3 turn DOM capture and evidence integration.

Why both DOM and vision?

DOM data can tell the agent that an element is a button, what its label is, and whether a select offers a desired option. A screenshot helps disambiguate spatial layout, visual labels, canvas-like interfaces, and controls whose semantic markup is weak. In V3, screenshot delivery depends on model capability and run policy.

Frames are not optional details
The scraper includes child-frame handling. A page can have the visible control inside an iframe; if an observation omits frames, the model may incorrectly conclude the target is absent.

ACTION LAYERPAGE 15 / 30

Action execution: from intent to browser effect

Once the model identifies a target and action, Skyvern converts that choice into a browser operation and records the result.

Navigation

Go to URL, back/forward, reload, switch tabs.

Pointer

Click, hover, move, drag, checkbox/radio interaction.

Text and keyboard

Type/fill text, press keys, paste, handle OTP fields.

Form selection

Select options, interact with custom selects and autocomplete suggestions.

Files

Upload files, initiate download, capture browser-delivered files.

Page utilities

Wait, scroll, inspect, extract, screenshot and validate.

Legacy step engine action path

The README exposes Playwright-like commands: page.click, page.fill, page.select_option, and page.upload_file. Each can use a selector, a natural-language prompt, or a selector-plus-AI fallback mode. The action handler contains more specialized handling for autocomplete commit evidence, download capture, OTP entry and browser failures.

Task V3 action path

V3 exposes thin raw-browser tools such as observe, click, type, select, scroll and file upload to the persistent loop. It resolves the live page for each call, enforces preflight/guard logic, and returns tool results to the model.

A good action must be observable
A click call returning without an exception does not always prove the business goal succeeded. The next observation and final goal check determine whether the intended state actually happened.

COMPOSITION MODELPAGE 16 / 30

Agents, workflows, blocks, and runs

A reusable agent/workflow is a saved sequence of blocks with defined inputs. A run is one execution of that saved automation.

Agent / Workflow

Saved reusable automation definition. The app calls it an Agent; older API/SDK vocabulary calls it a Workflow.

Block

A single operation or control-flow node: browser action, extraction, HTTP request, loop, conditional, and more.

Input

Named value supplied at run time: URL, query, account ID, credential reference, file URL, etc.

Run

One execution. Stores status, timeline, outputs, browser evidence and downloaded files.

Vocabulary mapping

AgentAPI/SDK concept: Workflow; identified by a workflow permanent ID.
InputsAPI/SDK concept: parameters.
Agent runAPI/SDK concept: workflow run, with its own run_id.

Why blocks?

Blocks make a larger automation understandable and reusable. The output from one block can be referenced by later blocks, so a run behaves like a dataflow graph with control-flow edges.

BLOCK CATALOGUE · PART 1PAGE 17 / 30

Browser automation blocks

These blocks use or control the live browser. Browser Task is the primary high-level action block.

Browser TaskNatural-language browser goal. The agent navigates and takes multiple actions until its goal is met.Use for multi-step navigation, form completion, and website tasks.
Browser ActionOne specified browser action, useful for a precise single click or input.Use when the next step is clear and narrow.
ExtractionReads the current page and returns structured information, optionally with a JSON Schema.Use for data capture, not writing form inputs.
LoginUses a saved credential and a login goal, including supported 2FA paths.Use when a site requires authentication.
Go to URLNavigates directly to a required URL without requiring the agent to reason about the destination.Use for deterministic entry points.
Print PagePrints the current browser page as a PDF artifact.Use for a rendered page snapshot or printable copy.

Block configuration fields

Browser blocks may include URL, engine, max-step override, 2FA identifier, verification URL, error-code mapping, completion criteria, complete-on-download, and a file name for a captured download. A blank URL can mean continue from the previously used page, where applicable.

Design rule
Put clear success criteria into the Browser Task prompt or the block’s “Complete if…” field. The model needs a testable definition of “done,” not just a vague instruction to keep going.

BLOCK CATALOGUE · PART 2PAGE 18 / 30

Data, file, and communication blocks

Not every workflow step needs a browser. Skyvern also processes files, queries systems, calls APIs, and communicates results.

Web Search

Searches Google/Exa via API; optional prompt/schema transforms results. It does not open each result in a browser.

Text Prompt

Sends text and prior outputs to an LLM for summarization, transformation or structured output.

File Parser

Parses PDF, CSV, Excel, images, DOCX and ZIP; outputs parsed records/files.

Google Sheets

Read rows/cells or append/update rows through a connected Google account.

HTTP Request

Calls REST endpoints with method, URL, headers, JSON body, timeout and optional file I/O.

PDF blocks

Fill fields in PDFs, split a PDF into documents, or export/print output files.

Send Email / Email Inbox

Send notifications or read/filter messages from connected Gmail/Outlook.

Cloud Storage

Transfer files to/from external object storage, where configured.

Human Interaction

Pause execution and ask a person to approve/reject or provide information.

Useful workflow pattern

Search or collect records → parse or normalize them → process with a prompt/code block → write to Sheets or call an HTTP API → send a summary email. Browser navigation and data operations can coexist in one workflow.

External integrations need setup
Google, Microsoft, SMTP, storage, and vault integrations depend on credentials and server configuration. A block existing in the schema does not mean every self-hosted installation has its integration keys configured.

HOW BRANCHES CONNECTPAGE 19 / 30

Control flow: conditions, loops, and stop rules

A workflow is not always a straight line. Conditional and loop blocks route execution based on values and tests.

Conditional

Each branch contains a condition expression. It may be a Jinja2 expression or a natural-language prompt. The first matching branch runs; an automatic Else branch catches cases where no condition matches.

Example: {'{'} extraction_output.price > 100 {'}'}

For each / While

For each processes a known list. Child blocks run once per item with current_value and 0-based current_index.

While re-checks a condition before every iteration. Useful for pagination, polling and retrying until a page state changes.

Other control blocks

AI Validation asserts a complete/terminate condition. Wait pauses for a defined duration. Terminate ends the run with a reason and optional error code. Code performs bounded custom Python processing. Agent Trigger starts another saved agent and may wait for it to finish.

DATA FLOW BETWEEN BLOCKSPAGE 20 / 30

Inputs, outputs, and templates

A reliable workflow makes data contracts explicit: inputs enter, blocks produce named outputs, and later blocks consume those outputs.

Run inputcustomer_id = "C-104"Typed parameter supplied by caller
↓
Block A outputfind_customer_outputStructured result from search/browser/extraction
↓
Block B input reference{'{'} find_customer_output.email {'}'}Template renders the previous output into the next step
↓
Final run outputoutputs + files + statusConsumed by UI, SDK, webhook, or another agent

Input types documented in Concepts

stringintegerfloatbooleanjsonfile_urlcredential_id

Reference syntax

Inputs are referenced as {'{'} input_key {'}'}. A block’s output is available to downstream steps as {'{'} block_label_output {'}'}. Inside a loop, current_value and current_index provide iteration context.

Why JSON Schema matters

When a model extracts information, a schema defines the keys and expected types. For example: product name as a string, price as a number, and availability as a boolean. A schema makes downstream conditions and API payloads more predictable; the output still needs validation against the schema.

Good design practice
Define the exact output fields before you write downstream blocks. Avoid asking a later block to infer a field name or type from a paragraph if you can provide a JSON schema.

SECRET HANDLINGPAGE 21 / 30

Credentials, login, and two-factor authentication

Skyvern separates the model’s reasoning about where a secret belongs from the secret value itself.

Credential vaultEncrypted saved username/password/card/secret
↓
Credential resolverSelects the credential and resolves required fields
↓
Masked model contextLLM sees a placeholder or redacted reference
↓
Browser inputSkyvern types the actual value into the intended field

Supported vault/service paths visible in the repo

Skyvern-managed credentials and adapters for Bitwarden, 1Password, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager, AWS Secrets Manager, and custom credential services. Specific vault availability depends on configuration and deployment.

2FA options

Authenticator / TOTPEmail codeSMS codePush approvalMagic linkPasskey

The credentials docs describe password credentials with optional 2FA setup. The workflow block can use a credential and identifier; OTP services and page tools handle code retrieval and safe entry. Task V3 also contains auth tools and TOTP placeholder resolution logic.

Never return secrets as output
The code and docs emphasize redaction in prompts, saved page data, logs, and screenshots. A workflow should not ask the model to echo a password or OTP in its final result. Transforming a secret can also make exact-match redaction harder, so pass it only where it is needed.

STATE MANAGEMENTPAGE 22 / 30

Database and persistence: what is stored?

Skyvern persists the definition of an automation separately from the execution records and evidence created by each run.

Workflow definitionSaved blocks, config, version, inputs
⇣
WorkflowRunOne run: status, request data, timing, parent/retry relationship
⇣
WorkflowRunBlockBlock-level execution/output
Task / TaskV2Task-specific state
Step / ActionDetailed execution timeline
Artifact / CredentialFile metadata and protected data

Data access stack

SQLAlchemy models map Python objects to relational tables. AgentDB composes repositories for workflows, runs, tasks, credentials, artifacts, sessions, schedules and feedback. Repositories isolate query operations. Alembic stores schema migrations and updates deployed databases.

Database options

The docs describe SQLite as the default for the pip quickstart and PostgreSQL for Docker Compose/production-style setups. The project includes PostgreSQL drivers and SQLite schema helpers.

Important distinction
The browser’s live page state is not the database. Persistent records let the UI and API inspect completed runs after the browser has moved on or closed.

RUN EVIDENCEPAGE 23 / 30

Artifacts, downloads, recordings, and webhooks

A run can produce much more than a final JSON response. Skyvern stores browser evidence and file outputs so a user can review or consume the result.

Screenshots

Visual evidence around page state and actions.

Recordings

Browser session video or action playback evidence.

Downloads

Files delivered by a website, parser, export or PDF block.

HAR / logs

Network and diagnostic evidence, subject to redaction/policy.

Artifacts

Metadata, signed links and storage references.

Webhook result

JSON event sent after a run ends.

Storage backends

local diskAmazon S3Azure Blob StorageGoogle Cloud Storage

The artifact storage factory selects a backend. In multi-server deployments, shared object storage is useful because a run may be inspected from another server and local disk is not automatically shared.

Webhook safety

Webhook payloads include run outcome data. The production docs describe an x-skyvern-signature HMAC-SHA256 header so the receiving application can verify that the body was signed with the Skyvern API key. Delivery retries and replay tools are part of the production story.

Evidence supports trust
A strong automation does not only say “done.” It should preserve the output, relevant screenshots/recording, and downloaded file so a person or downstream system can inspect what happened.

FASTAPI + SERVICE LAYERPAGE 24 / 30

Backend API architecture

The backend exposes REST routes and uses service objects to coordinate business logic, repositories, execution workers and browser operations.

Main layers

HTTP routesskyvern/forge/sdk/routes/ · request/response endpoints and auth dependencies
Service layerskyvern/services/ · prepare/run/cancel workflow, task, schedule, webhook, credential, file operations
Agent / engineskyvern/forge/agent.py · block dispatch and browser task execution
SDK / domain layerskyvern/forge/sdk/ · models, LLM handlers, workflow models, storage, DB, policy
InfrastructureDatabase, browser, LLM provider, object storage, external integrations

API application

create_api_app() creates a FastAPI app, initializes Forge services, configures CORS and middleware, mounts authenticated routers, sets exception handlers, and registers route aliases. The canonical API uses /v1; legacy prefixes such as /api/v1 and /api/v2 are also mounted for compatibility. Workflow routes are mirrored to agent aliases.

Why ForgeApp exists

ForgeApp is a shared dependency container holding the database, storage, cache, artifact manager, browser manager, LLM clients/handlers, credential vaults, workflow services, persistent-session manager and ForgeAgent.

Trace a request
When debugging an API problem, first find the route, then follow the called service, then the database repository or agent method. Avoid starting in a large engine file before you know which route and execution path were entered.

SDKs, MCP, and external integrations

The same platform can be driven from code, another AI client, or an automation platform.

Python SDK

Installed with pip install skyvern. The local extra enables a local browser/client mode; server extra installs the API server. Can connect to local API or Cloud.

from skyvern import Skyvern

TypeScript SDK

Published client under skyvern-ts/client / npm package @skyvern/client. Offers browser, page and agent methods.

import { Skyvern } from "@skyvern/client"

MCP

CLI MCP tools expose browser/session/workflow/credential capabilities to compatible clients. MCP is an integration interface, not the same thing as Task V3’s in-process raw-tool loop.

Automation connectors

Repository contains Make and n8n integration folders; README also mentions Zapier, Make and n8n workflows.

Higher-level agent methods

page.agent.run_task(), login(), download_files(), and run_workflow() let the caller hand off more complex sequences. Standard Playwright calls can be mixed with AI-powered prompt targeting.

Vision changes the browser observation

The selected model’s supports_vision property and screenshot policy determine whether the model receives page screenshots. A text-only model may rely on DOM/element observations; vision-capable models can use both. The self-hosted docs show Ollama settings and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint pattern.

Configuration example

ENABLE_OPENAI=true
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
LLM_KEY=OPENAI_GPT5_5

# Optional lower-cost model for lighter calls
SECONDARY_LLM_KEY=...
Do not hard-code one model assumption
The LLM key is configuration-driven and models evolve. The archive snapshot’s README and configuration registry are the source of truth for which model identifiers this exact checkout knows about.

SAFE EXECUTIONPAGE 28 / 30

Security and reliability boundaries

Browser automation can reach real accounts and modify real websites. The repo includes controls around secrets, URLs, run ownership, browser actions, and evidence.

Credential secrecy

Encrypt stored secrets when enabled; mask placeholders and redact known values in model-facing content, logs and artifacts.

Browser action policy

Pure decision logic evaluates evidence and action facts before allowing certain browser operations.

Network egress

Egress policy/monitoring controls which destinations a run can reach under configured authority and enrollment.

URL validation

Self-hosted docs describe optional blocking of loopback, private-network and cloud metadata addresses.

Run ownership

Database leases/session ownership and cancellation guards help prevent duplicate or stale workers from mutating a run.

Human approval

Human Interaction blocks can pause a run until approval/rejection or timeout.

Reliability is layered

Retries handle transient provider/network failures; page recovery can reacquire or reopen browser state; goal checks prevent premature completion; step, time and token budgets stop runaway loops; status finalization avoids overwriting a terminal state; artifacts preserve diagnostic evidence.

Self-hosted warning
Whoever can start a task may influence the URL opened by the browser. The self-hosted documentation warns that servers exposed to untrusted users should enable URL validation and must be protected with authentication/reverse-proxy controls.

Security review entry points

SECURITY.md, browser_action_policy.py, browser_egress_policy.py, credential_site_policy.py, encrypt/, secret_redaction.py, and the Task V3 tool preflight/credential release guards.

Practical contributor loop
Find the smallest relevant module → inspect existing tests → reproduce the behavior → write a focused test → make the smallest change → run formatting/lint/tests for the touched layer → open a PR with before/after evidence.

PUT THE PIECES TOGETHERPAGE 30 / 30

Complete walkthrough: download all recent invoices

A representative automation shows how inputs, browser tasks, extraction, loops, conditions, downloads, persistence, and webhooks connect.

Goal

“Open a vendor portal, sign in, find invoices newer than a chosen date, download each invoice, and return a structured report.”

1 · Input

portal_url, cutoff_date, credential_id.

2 · Login

Browser opens the portal and uses the chosen credential. 2FA can pause for or retrieve the required code.

3 · Navigate

Go to the invoice page and wait for the table to settle.

4 · Extract

Read invoice number, date, amount, row/link and download action using a data schema.

5 · Filter

Conditional logic checks whether each invoice date is newer than cutoff_date.

6 · Loop

For each matching invoice, click the download control and capture the resulting file.

7 · Process result

Record invoice metadata and downloaded file references; optionally write rows to Sheets or call HTTP API.

8 · Finalize

Verify expected downloads, return structured output, persist artifacts, and send a webhook/email report.

What to study in the code for each phase

docs/reference/blocks.mdxRead the block contract and configuration fields.
skyvern/services/workflow_service.pyUnderstand run preparation and dispatch.
skyvern/forge/agent.pyTrace block/task execution and engine routing.
skyvern/forge/taskv3/Understand browser tools, loop behavior and finish gates.
skyvern/webeye/Inspect browser actions, observation and download handling.
skyvern/forge/sdk/artifact/Trace artifact creation and storage.
Final takeaway
Skyvern is a coordinated platform: the workflow defines what should happen; the engine decides and executes; the browser performs real interactions; policy and verification constrain those interactions; persistence and artifacts make the result inspectable and reusable.

Check your understanding

  1. Why is a fresh page observation important after navigation?
  2. What is the difference between a browser session and a browser profile?
  3. When does Task V3 fall back to the step engine?
  4. Why is a JSON Schema useful after extraction?
  5. What evidence should support a completed status?
